text:
Maya (marketing): Heads-up — we have a latency spike in EU-west affecting generation endpoints. Ops is looking, but wanted to sync on customer-facing comms + timing.
Ethan (ops): Investigating. Looks like a noisy neighbor on a shared pool; impact ~15-25% of requests, higher tails. No data leak.
Priya (support): We're seeing ~40 tickets from customers in EU. Asking for a short status page message and recommended wording for CS templates.
Maya (marketing): Proposal: short status page now, email if >1 hour or large customers impacted. Avoid panic words — prefer "degraded performance" over "outage" unless it's total failure. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
Zoe (product): Agree on phrasing. For customers with reserved capacity, we should call out that Dedicated customers are not affected if that's true — confirm?
Ethan (ops): Dedicated pools unaffected. I'll confirm in 10 min.
Maya (marketing): Draft status copy below — please review quickly:

```
Status: Degraded performance in EU-west
We’re seeing increased latency for text generation requests in EU-west. Our engineers are investigating and mitigating. Users may experience slower responses; functionality remains available. We’ll post updates here and notify impacted customers directly.
```

Priya (support): Nice and calm. Add estimated next update time — set to 20 mins from now. Also add link to support form for high-priority tickets.
Maya (marketing): Updated snippet: "Next update: in 20 minutes. If you are experiencing critical impact, contact support: https://redwood.example.com/support"
Luca (legal): Quick note: don’t promise timelines we can’t keep. "Estimated" ok. Also avoid implying SLA credits.
Maya (marketing): Good catch. Tweaked to "Estimated next update" and removed any SLA language.
Ethan (ops): Confirmed: Dedicated unaffected. Impact is on hosted shared pools in EU-west.
Priya (support): CS template ready. Short DM to customers: "We're aware of slower responses in EU-west generation endpoints. We're investigating and will follow up within 20 minutes. If you see errors, please reply to this message with request IDs."
Maya (marketing): Should we send a public tweet/status post? Pro: transparency. Con: noise + attracts customers before fix. Recommendation: post status page first, wait one update cycle (20m). If persists, social broadcast.
Zoe (product): +1 wait for one update cycle. If we can isolate root cause quickly, avoid wider broadcast.
Maya (marketing): Action items:
- Ethan: confirm mitigation progress + update status in 20m (owner)
- Priya: start triage on tickets, notify impacted top 30 customers if errors (owner)
- Maya: draft status page + CS copy + internal short FAQ (owner)
- Luca: on-stand if wording escalates to legal scope

Please react with :thumbsup: if you’re aligned.
StatusBot: Incident created — INC-2026-18425. First ack by Ethan.
Ethan (ops): Quick update: rolling a kernel bump to the pool, expect improvement in ~7-10 mins.
Maya (marketing): If improvement within 10m, we’ll post "resolved" with brief postmortem link later. If not, escalate to email to customers + social.
Priya (support): Acknowledged. I’ll prepare an email draft in case.
Zoe (product): Also track any regressions on embeddings endpoints — different team but might be correlated.
Maya (marketing): Thanks everyone. Will push the status page copy now and set timer for 20 minutes.
Ethan (ops): Improvement visible in metrics at +8m, latency tail dropping. Will confirm once stable.
Priya (support): Tickets slowing, thanks.
Maya (marketing): :eyes: Good news — hold public social for now. Preparing follow-up note for customers about what happened and mitigation steps.
StatusBot: Incident INC-2026-18425 updated — status: monitoring.
Maya (marketing): Final note for thread: save the final status language for postmortem and marketing comms. We'll sync post-incident to craft the benchmark narrative updates if needed.
Ethan (ops): Marking incident as monitored.
Priya (support): Closing customer-facing loop — CS templates sent to team.
Maya (marketing): Thanks all — schedule 30-min postmortem check in 2 hours.
